label: Reset unit tracks the last seen state: high for S1 at D2, high after S2 at GO
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2)
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 34. The timing baseline (GO about 0.4, D2 about 0.2, D1 about 0.06) explains R^2 0.76. Beyond timing, the main driver is the state that was observed. At D2 it is much higher when the state just reached is S1 (+0.125), higher still when the previous trial was also rewarded (+0.07), and lower when this choice was a2 (-0.05) or the previous choice was a1 (-0.06). At GO the sign flips relative to state: it is higher after the previous trial reached S2 (+0.07), lower after an unrewarded S1 trial (-0.057), and falls a little as the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good rises (belief_lo, about -0.013 per log-odds unit). At D1 the effect is small: slightly higher after S2 (+0.025). The profile shows that the upcoming choice at GO (future: a2 high, a1 low) and the model policy (ref 0.38) track this. Previous-state and belief terms that the agent can observe replace them almost fully. Since no model outputs are used, observed-only terms lose very little. Recent reward alone, a marginal prev_reward term and the two-trial reward history added nothing. Some error remains after unrewarded streaks: D1 is under-predicted and GO / D2 after S1-unrewarded is over-predicted. 8 terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.797, test 0.792. Ceiling: all observed 0.91, all 0.93.

issues: The D1 claim is mis-attributed. Swapping (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) for (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) (equivalently in_rew == 0) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.792 to 0.808, and that term's weight goes up to +0.041. At D1 the unit tracks the reward that was not received, not the previous state. The misses output for the original terms agrees: D1 is under-predicted after a2 S1 u (+0.049) and after a1 S1 u (+0.020), so the error follows the unrewarded trials rather than S2.

The D2 claim 'lower when this choice was a2' only holds after controlling for the previous choice. In the raw residual table, a2-S1 at D2 (+0.128) is higher than a1-S1 (+0.090), and a2-S2 (-0.090) is higher than a1-S2 (-0.107). The negative weights on action==2 and prev_action==1 only come out together: with both terms the score is 0.792, with action==2 alone 0.740, with prev_action==1 alone 0.726. Read as a marginal statement, the claim points the wrong way.

The core state claims hold. Dropping D2*(state==S1) cuts the score to 0.665. GO*prev_state==2 beats GO*prev_action==2 (0.792 vs 0.744). Dropping the GO unrewarded-S1 term or the belief_lo term costs 0.022 and 0.065. The S1 x prev_reward term at D2 adds 0.032.

A gap remains: 0.79 to 0.81 against an all-observed ceiling of 0.91. The worst-fit windows are dominated by the first D1 of the episode (about 0.24 actual vs 0.045 predicted). Moderate systematic misses remain after the improved terms: GO after a2 S2 u is under-predicted by +0.037, D2 after a1 S2 r by +0.028, and D2 after a2 S2 u is over-predicted by -0.026.
